definitions.explanation: A baby or young pig. Used both in farming contexts and in stories, fairy tales, and as a term of endearment.

examples.japanese: {牧場|ぼくじょう}で{子豚|こぶた}に{触|さわ}ることができる。
examples.english: You can touch piglets at the farm.

examples.japanese: {三匹|さんびき}の{子豚|こぶた}の{話|はなし}は、{世界中|せかいじゅう}の{子供|こども}たちに{親|した}しまれている。
examples.english: The story of the three little pigs is beloved by children around the world.

notes:
A compound of {子|こ} (child; young) and {豚|ぶた} (pig), with rendaku changing ぶた to ぶた (the initial consonant does not change here since it is already voiced). Commonly encountered in the fairy tale {三匹|さんびき}の{子豚|こぶた} (The Three Little Pigs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子豚|こぶた}が{生|う}まれる: a piglet is born
- {三匹|さんびき}の{子豚|こぶた}: The Three Little Pigs
- {子豚|こぶた}を{育|そだ}てる: to raise piglets

RELATED TERMS:
- {豚|ぶた}: pig — the adult animal
- {子犬|こいぬ}: puppy — same {子|こ} prefix pattern
- {子猫|こねこ}: kitten — same {子|こ} prefix pattern
- {子牛|こうし}: calf — same {子|こ} prefix pattern
